en.html:
After a long absence, I presented myself before the Prince.
Before anything else, I bowed my head and apologized deeply.

ja.html:
久方ぶりに<ruby>罷<rt>まか</rt></ruby>り出た、親王の御前。
　俺は何をもさて置いて低頭し、深く謝した。
ja.text:
久方ぶりに罷まかり出た、親王の御前。

en.html:
Kageaki"Your Highness, Prince Maidono. ...The other day I caused you very great trouble. I offer my humblest apologies."
Chief"..."
Kageaki"After all your kindness, instead of repaying it I have repaid you with harm... With what face can I stand before you?"
舞殿宮"Bas, bas, Kageaki... Such a grown man, folding himself so small. That will not do."

舞殿宮 「ま、ま、景明くん……。 　大の男がそんな縮こまったらあかんえ」

en.html:
The voice from behind the blinds held no reproach. If anything, he was trying to soothe me.

But after what I had done, I could hardly think, ah, good, that was settled. Raising my head was not coming easily.

御簾の奥で発せられる声に叱責の調子はまるでなく、
むしろ宥める風であったが。
　己の所業を思えば、なら良かったと安堵もできない。
俺は容易に頭を上げられなかった。

Chief"I am deeply humbled."
舞殿宮"Though when I heard Kageaki had broken out of prison, I did spit out my tea..."
Kageaki"..."

His Highness remained entirely at ease.
For my part, I could not produce an answer.

ja.html: あくまで気楽な様子の親王に、言葉も返せない。

en.html:
舞殿宮"And for his tsurugi, no less. Admirable. A model warrior, this one..."
舞殿宮"Is he not, Chief?"
Chief"I am deeply humbled."
Kageaki"..."
舞殿宮"...Kikuchi... With you carrying on like that also, how is Kageaki to lift his head?"
Chief"Sir. But this happened because my supervision was inadequate—"
舞殿宮"Arre, bas! Is this an apology or a competition in who can fold himself smaller?"
舞殿宮"Everything ended without harm. So that is the end of this matter. Both of you understand?"
Chief"...Sir!"
Kageaki"..."

en.html:
The Prince, administrator of Hachiman Shrine, clapped his hands twice as he spoke.
The Chief and I bowed at exactly the same time. Neither had arranged it.

ja.html:
ぱんぱん、と手を打って言う八幡宮別当親王。
　俺と署長は期せずして同時に、一<ruby>揖<rt>ゆう</rt></ruby>した。
ja.text:

　俺と署長は期せずして同時に、一揖ゆうした。

en.html:
舞殿宮"...Ah, but Kageaki."
Kageaki"Sir."
舞殿宮"A word of thanks to the guard at the that place would be good. He did not make an unnecessary fuss. Thanks to him, we could keep this from becoming a large affair."
Kageaki"...I see."

I certainly owed him my thanks.
Really, how many people's hands did I keep occupied just by going on living?

Perhaps I had noticed rather late.

I had already reported Silver Star's announced attack on Hachiman Shrine. I had also urged that His Highness—and naturally the Chief—move elsewhere under some suitable pretext.

Was it about that?

　適当な口実を設けて親王には――当然署長にも――
遷居して頂くべきだと進言もしておいたが。

　その話か。

en.html:
Chief"No. That is urgent also, but... today we need to discuss something else."
Kageaki"Sir...?"
舞殿宮"All right, Kageaki? What we say now must not be repeated elsewhere..."
舞殿宮"Though with you, I hardly need to insist on that."
Chief"Still, Your Highness, given the nature of the matter... Kageaki."
Kageaki"Sir. Whatever you tell me, I promise that I shall never repeat it."
舞殿宮"Yes, yes. When someone like you says it, Kageaki, one can breathe easily."

en.html:
The Prince laughed softly. But there was tension in the laughter too.

It seemed to be something considerable.
...Political, probably. After all.

But why take the trouble to tell me?
